newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end weaker in further consolidation.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end weaker in further consolidation.

text.p: French stocks finished the week with a third day of measured consolidation on Friday after a run of record-setting sessions.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended down 12.40 points or 0.48 percent at 2562.84 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down six at 2,576.0.
Volume was a healthy 9.9 billion francs on monthly settlement day.
*Insurer AGF was the most heavily traded stock of the session, rising 3.41 percent with 2.7 million shares changing hands.

Stock enters CAC-40 on Monday and was also helped by renewed speculation after German bank Merck, Finck & Co published study on Thursday saying now could be a good time for a takeover move by Germany's Allianz AG.
*Small bank Worms & Cie soars 10.87 percent amid renewed speculation of it selling insurer Athena.

After market closed, Worms & Cie and Saint Louis said in a joint statement they planned a full merger in which Saint Louis would be absorbed into Worms. Deal based on four Worms shares for one Saint Louis share.

Worms, which already owned more than 67 percent, also said it planned to raise its dividend to 9.50 francs a share from eight francs and said the merger would not be dilutive for shareholders in terms of net asset value and earnings per share.
*BIC, weaker, and Valeo, stronger, are two other CAC-40 entrants which made up much of Friday trading along with AGF.

*Club Med whose shares were suspended pre-open and closed at 355.5 francs on Thursday, announced after closure that it would produce a net loss of 743 million francs for 1995/96 after charges of 820 million francs due to a major restructuring to restore profitability.
Philippe Bourguignon of Euro Disney, whose share was weaker, will move to Club Med as chief executive. Current boss Serge Trigano to become head of a supervisory board.

* Cie Bancaire ends higher, lifted both by continued speculation it could be sold by Paribas and also by positive readout from analysts meeting despite reporting loss of 1.23 billion for 1996 on Thursday, including provisions of 2.48 billion francs.
"All the loss areas will be cleaned up in 1997," said one dealer.
* Other financials, BNP, CCF also closed higher.
